chunks: Al-Shaykh al-Jalil Abu Ja‘far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ahmad al-Daqqaq (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Harun al-Sufi narrated to us. He said: Ubaydullah b. Musa al-Habbal al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn al-Khashab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Muhsin narrated to us from Yunus b. Thibyan from al-Sadiq Ja‘far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): Why do I see you alone? He said: I have abandoned the people, and they have abandoned me for Your sake. He said: Then why do I see you silent? He said: My awe of You has silenced me. He said: Then why do I see you exhausted? He said: Loving You has exhausted me. He said: Then why do I see you poor when I have enriched you? He said: Fulfilling my duty to You has impoverished me. He said: Then why do I see you humbled? He said: The greatness of Your majesty, which cannot be described, has humbled me; and that is rightfully Yours, O my Master. Allah, glorified is His majesty, said: So rejoice with the bounty from Me, for you shall have whatever you desire on the Day you meet Me. Associate with the people, and treat them with good manners, and distinguish yourself from them in their deeds, and you shall attain what you want from Me on the Day of Resurrection.

And al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Allah, mighty and glorified, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): O Dawud! Rejoice by Me, seek pleasure by remembering Me, and seek enjoyment by speaking to Me. Soon, I will empty the abode of the transgressors, and I will place My curse upon the oppressors.

key_terms.جَلَالِكَ: Your majesty; the overwhelming grandeur and glory of Allah that surpasses description
key_terms.خَشْيَتُكَ: Awe or reverential fear of You (Allah); a spiritual station where the servant is overcome by the magnitude of the divine
key_terms.مُتَذَلِّلًا: Humbled or abased; a state of complete self-abasement before the majesty of Allah
key_terms.مُنَاجَاتِي: My intimate conversation; private, secret discourse between the servant and Allah in prayer
key_terms.نَصِبًا: Exhausted or fatigued; used here to describe the physical and spiritual toll of love for Allah
key_terms.وَحْدَانًا: Alone or solitary; Dawud's state of seclusion, having withdrawn from people for Allah's sake

ai.seo_question: What did Allah reveal to Prophet Dawud about solitude, divine love, and engaging with people according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated in the Thirty-Sixth Assembly of al-Shaykh al-Saduq's Amali sessions, presents a divine dialogue between Allah and Prophet Dawud (AS). In the first revelation, Allah questions Dawud about his solitude, silence, exhaustion, poverty, and humility. Dawud's answers reveal the inner states of a devoted servant: he abandoned people for Allah's sake, was silenced by awe, exhausted by love, impoverished by duty, and humbled by divine majesty. Allah rewards his sincerity with glad tidings and instructs him to engage with people outwardly while remaining distinct in conduct. In a second revelation, Allah invites Dawud to find joy in Him, pleasure in His remembrance, and enjoyment in intimate prayer, promising to purge the world of evildoers.
